# Error catalog

You are holding an error class — a string from an event, a terminal signal, or
an API response — and you want to know what produced it, whether an
`error_types` entry can act on it, and what to change. Find the literal string
in the index below and open its page.

If you are writing error routing rather than diagnosing a failure, start with
**[routing.md](routing.md)**. Three things about routing surprise most authors:

- **The lookup is an exact string match.** A bare `*` entry catches nothing. A
  `http/*` entry catches nothing. Enumerate the classes you mean.
- **The default is fail-fast.** A class with no matching entry gives up and
  settles the run failed. Retry is opt-in, everywhere.
- **The vocabulary is per-deployment and unversioned.** Which classes are
  recognised depends on which peers this deployment configures and which
  executor a node names. There is no versioned catalog and no deprecation
  marker anywhere in the capabilities handshake.

### Advertised families, which are not classes

Five strings ending in `/*` appear in what an executor advertises. They exist
so that `error_types` keys beneath the prefix register without a warning. **No
failure ever carries one of them**, and an `error_types` key spelled with the
wildcard never fires. Route the concrete class listed above instead.

| Advertised | Concrete class you must key on |
| --- | --- |
| `agent/subprocess_exit/*` | `agent/subprocess_exit/before_complete` |
| `agent/tool_use_failed/*` | `agent/tool_use_failed/<tool>` |
| `http/request_invalid/*` | `http/request_invalid/<upstream class>`, `http/request_invalid/_unspecified` |
| `http/server_error/*` | `http/server_error/<status>` |
| `verifier/check_failed/*` | `verifier/check_failed/<name>` |

`acquire/*` is the same trap from the other direction: the validator accepts
it silently, because anything under `acquire/` counts as runtime-synthesized,
and it still routes nothing.

## Finding the class you have

The class is the tail of the event kind. `GET /v1/events?kind=<kind>` matches
the kind **exactly** — a prefix matches nothing.

| Outcome | Event kind |
| --- | --- |
| Terminal failure | `terminal/error/<class>` |
| In-place retry | `transient/retry/<n>/<class>` |
| Release and requeue | `transient/release_and_requeue/<class>` |
| Dispatch fault | `transient/infra/<class>` |
